answer: Hardware prism attestation: each identity must run inside its own $35 secure-enclave chip with a unique burned-in key — $35 and one chip per fake, no bulk discount. The kernel inside the chip signs a fresh challenge nonce each epoch, and the single registration inlet checks the signature against a public registry of issued chips; a duplicate chip fingerprint or a replayed nonce is rejected on the spot. A 1,000-fake farm needs 1,000 chips and $35,000 in hardware, and one chip cannot pretend to be two identities. Limit: stolen chips could be reused, so chip age is capped at 2 years.
